phase_name: GLP-001 Governance Lifecycle Pattern Contract Freeze
summary: Contract-freeze phase converting Phase 137V's evidence-derived Governance Lifecycle Pattern architecture into GLP-001 v1.0, the normative Governance Lifecycle Pattern Contract (docs/contracts/GOVERNANCE_LIFECYCLE_PATTERN_CONTRACT.md). Defines a mandatory four-stage core (Architecture, Contract Freeze, Implementation, Independent Verification) and two conditional stages (Repository-Wide Hardening, Certification), each with objective, required outputs, responsibilities, entry criteria, exit criteria, and evidence expectations traced to 137V. Defines objective applicability criteria (favoring and excluding GLP designation), a proportionality contract distinguishing major architectural initiatives from routine implementation work, per-role responsibilities (Architecture authors, Contract authors, Implementers, Independent verifiers, Hardening owners, Certification authorities, Human authority), a per-stage evidence contract, and a two-scope verification model separating Subsystem Verification (Scope A) from Governance Execution Verification (Scope B) -- the latter directly operationalizing 137V's Population-B finding that a track's own verification stages do not automatically cover the harness's own finalization/reporting meta-tooling. Defines a four-outcome compliance model (Compliant / Partially compliant / Not applicable / Non-compliant) that explicitly accommodates 'CONDITIONALLY CLOSED' as a legitimate Certification verdict. States compatibility (complements, does not replace, existing governance; no retrospective invalidation of any prior initiative), extensibility (additive-only future revisions), and security considerations (no runtime/execution/authority capability introduced). Records the four alternative lifecycle shapes 137V considered and why GLP-001 adopts the four-stage-core-plus-two-conditional-stages model rather than the 3-stage or unconditional 6-stage alternatives. Includes an 18-row traceability matrix mapping every major obligation back to its specific 137V section and citation. No lifecycle rule was invented beyond what 137V's evidence supports. No implementation. No governance behavior changes. No production code. No lifecycle enforcement introduced. Runtime remained Observed / observe / unavailable throughout.
